newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish court jails pro-Chechen ferry hijackers.
newsitem.headline: Turkish court jails pro-Chechen ferry hijackers.

text.p: A Turkish security court on Friday sentenced nine pro-Chechen gunmen to more than eight years in jail each for hijacking a packed Russian ferry last year in protest at Moscow's military crackdown in Chechnya.
"Five years for hijacking the ferry, three years and 10 months for violating the freedom of others," judge Ali Demir said, reading out the sentence after convicting the nine.

The defendants -- six Turks, two Chechens and an ethnic Abkhaz from Georgia -- chanted "Allahu Akbar" (God is Greatest) and scuffled with police after the sentence was announced. One of them shouted "You are dead" at the judge.
Defence lawyers say the hijackers will probably serve only 3 1/2 years because time served in custody considerably reduces the final sentence.

The hijackers seized the 3,838-ton Russian ferry Avrasya in January, 1996 from the Turkish Black Sea port of Trabzon. They had threatened to blow up the boat and its 200 passengers but the incident ended peacefully in Istanbul four days later.
Defence lawyer Ethem Baykal said the hijackers had not threatened Turkish interests. "They flew the Turkish flag on the mast of the ship. This is a sign of their loyalty to this country," he said.
Many Turks are sympathetic to the Chechen cause because of religious and historical links to the Caucasus area.
